counterfactual_missing_items: No troponin elevation, wall-motion abnormality, or pericardial effusion is reported; mild diastolic dysfunction does not establish cardiac injury
No fever or hypoxia is documented; PCR and crackles alone do not make pneumonia the central diagnosis
No atrial flutter waves, AV dissociation, or pre-excitation pattern is described; the regular long-RP narrow-complex tachycardia is the rhythm-specific evidence
decisive_items: Regular, narrow complex tachycardia with rate of 170 beats/min
Superiorly directed P waves (negative in leads II, III, and aVF)
Long RP interval (RP interval > PR interval)
response.rationale: R2 is the only candidate whose raw support spans directly encode the ECG diagnosis: regular narrow-complex tachycardia, superiorly directed P waves, and a long RP interval. R1 and R4 rely on nonspecific pulmonary/echo findings and omit the tachyarrhythmia; R3 mentions arrhythmia only in the generator assessment, not in raw spans, and its cited spans are solely COVID/respiratory. Therefore the ECG-specific atrial tachycardia is the best-supported diagnosis.

rejected.why: Raw spans support COVID-19 pneumonia (PCR, crackles) but do not account for the regular narrow-complex tachycardia or P-wave/RP-interval findings.
Raw support includes only COVID-19 positivity and respiratory symptoms; no ECG or tachycardia span is supplied, so the arrhythmia component is unsupported by raw evidence.
Mild diastolic dysfunction is nonspecific and is not raw evidence of acute cardiac injury; the decisive ECG findings of atrial tachycardia are not cited.
